newsitem.title: UK: Yahoo! UK says Internet users not "lonely nerds".
newsitem.headline: Yahoo! UK says Internet users not "lonely nerds".

text.p: Yahoo! UK, a provider of Internet search engines, on Thursday said a new survey dispels the myth that Internet users are "lonely nerds," showing them instead to be active, affluent adults who use the Internet for work and leisure.
"The 'lonely nerd' stereotype is now invalid," Yahoo! UK said in the survey results. "They are affluent, well-read adults with careers, homes and families who live life to the full."

The survey, conducted by Continental Research for Yahoo! UK, showed that 59 percent of the service's users are aged 25 to 44, 83 percent are part of households comprising two or more people, and 54 percent have families.
The average income for Yahoo! users in households of more than two people is 44,000 pounds, more than three times the national average.

According to the survey of 1,258 respondents, 85 percent use the Internet in the office and at home, 97 percent communicate by email, 73 percent use the Internet daily, and 59 percent spend at least six hours a week using the Internet.

As a result of spending time on the Internet, 56 percent of respondents said they watch less television; 52 percent said they send fewer letters and memos; 30 percent spend less time reading newspapers, 28 percent talk less on the telephone, 21 percent spend less time reading magazines, and 15 percent reported working less.
